headline: Council approved $1.1 million for police cruisers and body cameras and $1.5 million to hire 14 firefighters.
summary: Council approved $1.1 million in free cash for police cruisers and body cameras, and $1.5 million to hire 14 firefighters. It asked for a public Flock camera demonstration and a report on a senior property tax freeze. It also approved a letter opposing any shelter use of the ICC building.
decisions: Approved asking city departments to work with community partners to find underused public space downtown.
Approved asking for information on when Bicentennial Park on Jackson Street will open.
Withdrawn: motion to send the $1.1 million police funding transfer to a finance subcommittee.
Approved transferring $1.1 million in free cash to the Lowell Police Department for police cruisers and body cameras, 7-3.
Approved a $1.5 million supplemental appropriation to the Fire Department to hire 14 firefighter recruits; nine yes votes were read on roll call.
Referred the request about a tree leaning toward 38 Fox Street to the city manager and DPW for a report and recommendation.
Approved asking the city manager to have the proper department address the on-ramp from Centerville to the Hunts Falls Rotary, including signage.
Approved a motion to have the clerk prepare the executive session minutes on the Flock discussion, to be voted on for release later, 8-2.
Approved asking the city manager to arrange a public Flock camera demonstration with a question-and-answer session.
Approved sending a letter stating opposition to using the ICC building for any type of shelter.
Approved asking the city manager for a report on the yearly cost of a property tax freeze for residents over 75 who have owned and lived in their home more than 30 years.
Referred the minimum residential factor for fiscal 2027 to a public hearing on November 10, 2026 at 7 p.m.
Approved asking the state to approve plan changes for 278 Middlesex Street to support private redevelopment, 10-0.
Failed motion to cut the PEG fund transfer by $28,430 to $152,000.
Approved transferring $180,430 from PEG access funds for various technology improvements, 7-2.
Referred item 8.1, a claim for property damage, for a report and recommendation.
Referred gas and utility work requests 8.3 to 8.6 to a public hearing on November 5.
discussion: Members asked why the police cruiser and body camera costs were not in the budget. Some asked to send the $1.1 million transfer to a finance subcommittee first, and that motion was withdrawn before the vote.

Members asked whether 14 new firefighters would reduce the $4 million overtime budget. Officials said the hires would not stop company closures right away, and that the effect on overtime would be seen later.

Public speakers raised privacy and oversight concerns about Flock cameras. Members discussed a public demonstration with questions and answers, and whether executive session minutes should be released.
Members discussed the PEG fund transfer and whether to give more money to LTC while its workforce contract is still being negotiated. A motion to cut $28,430 failed.
Members and residents discussed the ICC building, including concern about a possible homeless shelter. The council sent a letter stating opposition to any shelter use.
